FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A01
Night front bicycle lights are mandatory white, while rear red lights are optional extras beside the mandatory rear reflectors. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A01
Spoke reflectors sit near the rim in white or amber at the front wheel and amber or red at the rear, while sidewall reflection covers the tire sides. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A01
A right turn across a cyclist waits for the rider to yield or pass, while a cyclist should pass motorists on the left. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A01
Many bicyclists younger than fifteen have neither taken a bicycle safety course nor passed the motor vehicle test, leaving them unaware of many road rules and requiring extra caution around young riders [A01].
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A01
A parked car must clear travel lanes and stay visible both ways, while a roadway park hugs the curb or shoulder edge. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A02
Vehicles parked on a roadway or shoulder during darkness must display front and rear lights visible from five hundred feet, and any headlights left on must be dimmed [A02].
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A02
Leaving a space signals and scans both ways, while backing out adds a double-check for bikes and walkers. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A02
Downhill parking aims wheels at the curb, while uphill parking aims them away, or away from the street without a curb. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A02
Parallel parking aligns two feet out with bumpers even, then cuts right to forty-five degrees before swinging left into the space. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A03
White curbs serve passenger stops and yellow curbs attended loading, while red curbs ban every stop. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-R11 | anchor: A03
Hydrants need fifteen feet and crossings fifty, while signals and signs need thirty and intersection crosswalks twenty. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-R12 | anchor: A03
Same-side fire driveways need twenty feet clear, while opposite-side driveways need seventy-five. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec08-R13 | anchor: A04
Minimum coverage splits per person, per accident and for property, while evidence must ride along in the vehicle always. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-R14 | anchor: A04
A first uninsured offense draws fine or jail plus points, while repeat offenses add plate and registration suspension. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-R15 | anchor: A04
Self-insurer status fits large fleets, while non-residents rely on adequate in-state policies or lose privileges. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0057]

FACT_ID: sec08-R16 | anchor: A04
Crash nonpayment suspends automatically for up to six years, while the verification system confirms coverage in real time. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0057]
